$comment: Project Managers: supervisors with a name and a memory. Rust reads it in supervisor::managers, supervisor::memory and machine tests (include_str!), TypeScript in src/lib/agents/supervisorManagers.ts. Change this first, then both sides.

names.$comment: Trimmed before the checks. Unique among non-archived managers ignoring case (manager_name_taken).

keyFromName.$comment: Fold to ASCII, lowercase, every run of other characters becomes one '-', trim dashes, cut to 48 (then trim a trailing dash again). Empty becomes 'manager'. A key that is taken (any registry entry, archived included, or a live supervisor) or reserved (supervisorLink.fixtures.json supervisorKeys.reservedPattern) gets -2, -3, ... appended, cut so the whole stays within 48.

promotionKey.$comment: Which key a promoted run ends up with: the live supervisor's key, else the key its supervisor.json names, else keyFromName(name). A run that already has an address keeps it.

cases.$comment: otherLiveKeys: keys of live supervisors working elsewhere. The remembered key is theirs now, so it is not taken.
cases.name: Inbox

launchKey.$comment: admit_supervisor for a registry holding the managers below. resume: the run folder name a launch resumes, or null for a new supervisor. own: the key the launch names. result: the key it runs under, the folder a new launch turns into a resume of, or the refusal code. live: supervisors already running, as in agentControl.fixtures.json supervisors.

cases.$comment: fileKey: the key the resumed folder's supervisor.json remembers. A manager's key there does not make a plain resume a manager.

refusals.$comment: Code -> sentence pattern. Rust produces the sentence, the frontend recognises the code by the pattern, as supervisors.runDirInUse does in agentControl.fixtures.json.
refusals.manager_name_invalid: ^A Project Manager name needs 1 to 40 characters on one line\.$
refusals.manager_run_missing: ^The supervisor run folder '.+' no longer exists\.$
refusals.manager_run_taken: ^The run folder .+ already belongs to the Project Manager '.+'\.$
refusals.manager_key_mismatch: ^The run folder .+ belongs to the Project Manager '.+' and runs only under its key '.+'\.$
refusals.manager_key_foreign_folder: ^The key '.+' belongs to the Project Manager '.+' and runs only its own run folder\.$
refusals.manager_archived: ^The Project Manager '.+' is archived\. Restore it before opening it\.$
refusals.manager_not_archived: ^The Project Manager '.+' must be archived before it is removed\.$
refusals.instructions_too_large: ^INSTRUCTIONS\.md of '.+' is \d+ bytes; the limit is 16384\.$
refusals.registry_unreadable: ^supervisor-managers\.json could not be read: .+ It was left as it is\.$
refusals.manager_create_failed: ^Could not create a run folder for '.+': .+$
refusals.human_drafting: ^The human is typing in this terminal; the message was not sent\.$

instructions.$denyRulesVerified: Claude Code 2.1.308, 2026-10-22, claude -p with --tools Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Bash --restricted --allowedTools Read Write Edit Glob Grep "Bash(sleep *)" --permission-mode dontAsk. Refused: Edit by relative path, Write by absolute path, Write through sub/../INSTRUCTIONS.md, and the Bash command 'sleep 1 && echo changed > INSTRUCTIONS.md'. Without the deny rules the same Edit went through (control). The rule matches the file name at any depth: sub/INSTRUCTIONS.md was refused too, with or without './'. Only print mode was run; the interactive TUI uses the same permission rules but was not checked.

memory.$comment: The OKF bundle a manager keeps. Layout check = our contract (always runs, needs no tool). okf check = okf validate on the same folder when okf is installed (machine.okf).
memory.logFormat: One '## YYYY-MM-DD' heading per day, newest first, entries as '* **<Kind>**: <sentence>' (what okf init and okf create write).
memory.sectionIndex: index.md without front matter: '# <Section>' then one '* [<title>](<file>.md) - <description>' line per concept (what okf create maintains).

layoutFindings.$comment: What the layout check reports, per concept file in a section folder. okf v0.7.0 itself does not report broken_front_matter (an unterminated quote passed as a concept) or dangling_superseded_by.

scanTruncated.$comment: Not a per-file code: the walk stopped at its file budget, so counts and findings are incomplete. Reported first, without a path.

okf.$comment: Captured 2026-10-22 in src-tauri/src/machine/testdata/okf-*.txt, bundles in testdata/okf-bundles/. Installed with go install (Go 1.25.6, GOTOOLCHAIN=auto building with go1.26.0). The binary landed in ~/go/bin, which is not on this Mac's login-shell PATH.

exitCodes.0: conformant (warnings, broken links and orphans may still be present)
exitCodes.2: bundle could not be loaded; output is plain text even with --json

jsonFields.$comment: broken_links and orphans are null, not [], when empty. warnings stayed [] while the text output listed warnings; findings live in errors, gate_findings, broken_links and orphans.

go.$comment: okf's go.mod asks for go 1.26.0; Go 1.21+ fetches that toolchain itself under GOTOOLCHAIN=auto.

create.$comment: manager_create { name }: a Project Manager without an earlier run. Rust creates a fresh run folder under the runs root exactly as a new supervisor launch names it, then runs promotion steps 3-6 on it (name rules, key from the name, INSTRUCTIONS.md and knowledge/ templates, append). If a promotion step refuses, the empty folder is removed again, so a refused name leaves nothing behind. A folder that cannot be created is manager_create_failed.

runMissing.$comment: A manager whose runDir no longer resolves under the runs root stays in manager_list with runMissing: true instead of disappearing. The UI says 'Folder missing', offers no Open, Ask or Edit Instructions, and offers Archive (active) or Remove (archived). Open by key answers manager_run_missing.

lastSession.$comment: Where a manager stands, without reading its terminal: the newest non-deprecated concept in knowledge/sessions/, as the manager wrote it. Newest by generated.at (RFC 3339) when it parses and is not later than the file's modification time plus one day, else by the modification time, so a model-written future date cannot pin an old note. index.md is not a concept; a file with missing or broken front matter is not a session. Part of manager_memory's summary as lastSession: { title, description, atMs, path } or null.

cases.name: a model-written future date cannot pin an old note
a time zone offset is compared as the instant it is
mtime when generated is absent or unreadable
broken front matter is not a session

sessionEnd.$comment: One inbox notification per ended manager session, after that session's memory check. A session is identified by its start, the registry field session.startedAt, booked on every manager start including a restore after an app restart (lastLaunch is not it: it stays the hash of the injected prompt and a restore books none). Exit and kill note it when they happen and set session.notedAt = startedAt; a session that ended with an app quit, a crash or power loss is caught up on the next app start: any non-archived manager whose session.startedAt is set and whose notedAt differs from it. An entry without the field is not caught up. The dedupe key uses the start, the one thing both paths know. Never a toast: a finished session is not an alarm. 'Wrote a note' is decided by file time, never by a model-written timestamp: the newest session concept whose modification time is >= the session start floored to the whole second. Its description (else its title) is the body, cleaned of control characters and cut to bodyMaxChars; with no such note the body says so plainly. The problem count is the full count before the prompt cap, scan_truncated not counted; a truncated scan says 'at least'. The action opens the manager on a click; it carries no task and no launch.
sessionEnd.title: <name> finished a session
sessionEnd.bodyWithoutNote: <name> ended this session without writing a session note.

openManagerAction.$comment: Notification and schedule action that opens a Project Manager, optionally with a task. A task goes to a running manager as one message (sendAgentInput: bracketed paste + Enter), to a stopped one as the first task of the resume. launch 'auto' starts on arrival only for a user-authored payload (dispatcher system or ui) whose occurrence is fresh (isFreshOccurrence), exactly as run-skill, and never switches the open project. The MCP notify vocabulary does not accept open-manager at all: a model must not hand another long-lived agent a task, not even behind a click.

autoDelivery.$comment: A task delivered without a click (launch auto) to a running manager is sent with automatic: true. Rust refuses it with human_drafting while the human has unsent text in that terminal (the same HumanDrafts the pingback respects), and never books automatic text as human keystrokes. On that refusal, and whenever an automatic start would need a dialog (provider choice), nothing happens: the notification stays unread with its button. A click is never refused this way.

ask.$comment: 'Ask <name>…' is the one way to hand a manager work from a tile, the rail or Settings. Same delivery as openManagerAction's task. With a task the start prompt still has the manager read its memory first, then work on that task without waiting for a go-ahead for it; anything beyond the task still waits. Empty or whitespace-only text is no task: Send stays disabled with a reason.

presentation.$comment: App pref auric.supervisor.managers, keyed by manager key. model is optional: absent means the supervisor default (Rust's smallest ranked allowed model). A model is a launch option, never a grant: rank and modelReason rules apply unchanged; a model the provider no longer offers is dropped and the default used.
